subject: Echo AI — Post-call: perf targets, context window & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@echo.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@echo.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Echo AI — Post-call: perf targets, context window & next steps

Thanks again for your time today — good discussion. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we all have the same expectations heading into the technical deep-dive:

Recap of perf/qual targets you shared:
- Target P95 generation latency: 120ms (interactive UI flows, streaming allowed)
- Target cold-start p95: ~200ms (acceptable with warm cache fallback)
- Sustained throughput target: 200 requests/sec across peak region (US-West)
- Concurrency target: Support 250 concurrent sessions with per-session KV cache
- Context window requirement: up to 8,192 tokens total (typical input ~5k, output ~3k), but 90% of requests are <=2k input tokens
- Streaming: required for UI (progressive partial tokens) — important to preserve token ordering and connectors to our websocket layer

Immediate asks from Redwood to help size a pilot and SLO proposal:
1) Can you share a representative sample of prompts and response size distribution (anonymized) — 2–3 example conversations plus a QPS histogram if possible.
2) Any existing perf baselines (p95/p99) with current model/provider? (you mentioned a summary table in the call)
3) Network topology (ingress region, single/multi-region, expected cross-region failover) — we may need the network-diagram to estimate RTT impact.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short template (Echo_Root_SLOs.xlsx) that maps the SLOs you mentioned into metrics we’ll use for the pilot (latency buckets, throughput, error budget). Please fill the second tab with the QPS and token-distribution if you can.

Proposed next steps (please confirm availability):
- Tech deep-dive with infra + runtime engineers: 60min — suggested Wednesday 2026-11-04 09:00 PT (I’ll send invite once Anita confirms).
- We’ll propose 2 pilot configurations: Hosted+edge caching (lower setup time) and Dedicated quantized 8k-context (best latency at scale).
- Deliverable: pilot plan + cost/perf tradeoffs and an acceptance test harness (we’ll include a shared script for running QPS/latency tests).

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once we lock the time. Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0112
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@echo.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@echo.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Echo AI — Post-call: perf targets, context window & next steps

Hi Jordan — thanks for the crisp recap. Confirming the items you listed and adding a bit more color:

- Streaming: yes, streaming is required for our main agent UI. We need token-level flushing (partial) to the frontend and an ordered stream; out-of-order chunks are a UX issue.
- Typical payloads: average input token size ~520 tokens (but we have long form templates that go up to ~5k). Output averages 150 tokens but heavy reports can be 2–3k.
- Baseline: attached a short internal perf summary (echo-internal-perf-summary.pdf) with our current provider numbers — 95th historically around 180ms for 512-token requests, tail worsens with longer contexts.
- Network: primary region is us-west-2 with a DR region in us-east-1. Diagram attached (network-diagram.pdf).

We can share a sanitized CSV with QPS by hour for the last 30 days and a couple of redacted prompt examples. Give me an SFTP or Drive folder and we’ll drop the files by EOD tomorrow.

One clarification: when you say "cold-start p95 ~200ms," are you assuming warm prefix cache or absolutely cold worker spin-up? Our preference is safe upper-bounds for absolute cold starts.

Available for the deep-dive on Wed 11/4 09:00 PT — please send an invite with the agenda and list of attendees on the infra/runtime side.

Thanks — Anita

--
Anita Shah
Director of Platform Engineering | Echo AI
anita.shah@echo.ai | +1 (206) 555-0199
(Attachment: echo-internal-perf-summary.pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 18:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Echo AI — Post-call: perf targets, context window & next steps

Quick internal note — wiring up options before the deep-dive so we can be crisp: 

Topline options to present:
1) Hosted + edge prefix caching
   - Pros: fastest time-to-pilot, stream support, lower upfront cost
   - Cons: slightly higher per-token unit cost at peak; cold-start tail depends on warm pool sizing
   - Pilot scope: configurable warm pool + prefix KV cache, run 24h soak with customer QPS trace

2) Dedicated reserved capacity (quantized 8k runtime)
   - Pros: best P95 at scale, predictable latency and unit cost; can guarantee concurrency targets with reserved slots
   - Cons: longer setup, contractual commit needed for reserved GPU capacity
   - Pilot scope: 2-week dedicated cluster, acceptance test with 200 RPS sustained and streaming validation

Technical asks for both tracks:
- Example prompts + QPS histogram (Anita to provide)
- Clarify absolute cold-start SLA expectations (spin-up vs warm pool)
- Streaming protocol details (we need details on your websocket layer and message framing)

I’ll prep a short decision matrix and cost delta table for the deep-dive. Rishi — would you mind pulling rough kernel/runtime cost estimates for quantized 8k vs 4k so we can show ballpark $/1M tokens?

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Anita — appreciate the attachments. I created a shared Drive folder and uploaded the Echo_Root_SLOs.xlsx template so you can drop the CSV there: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bEchoAI-Perf

Agenda for the Wed 11/04 09:00 PT deep-dive (60min):
- 5m: Introductions & goals
- 10m: Echo perf baseline walkthrough (Anita)
- 20m: Redwood architecture options + tradeoffs (Marissa + Rishi)
- 15m: Streaming & integration constraints (Priyom + Vivek)
- 10m: Pilot plan, next milestones, and owner assignments

I’ve sent the calendar invite to the attendees (link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=deepdive-echo-tech). Priyom/Vivek — please join with short notes on streaming framing and how we’ll validate token-order guarantees.

Deliverable timeline: Redwood will circulate a one-page pilot plan within 48 hours post-deep-dive, and a draft SOW within 7 business days if we align on the Dedicated pilot.

Jordan
